correctness.rationale: For every representation and marked chord set, gap-parity profiles are exactly symmetric differences of prefix masks. There are at most \(\binom{2m}{2}+1\) patterns, even for original marked vertices. The explicit word has exactly endpoint singleton masks and every consecutive length-two/length-three mask; all their XORs are classified by at most two binary runs. The complete placements table, valid for arbitrary \(m\ge7\), sums to \(2m^2-4m+1\), and the \(m=5,6\) boundary is exhaustively checked. Independent geometric crossing and mask formulations are checked through \(m=22\); the same exact word count and run table are checked through \(m=36\) and all chord diagrams up to \(m=6\). These finite computations are confirmatory, not infinity proofs.

broader_coverage.reasoning: The Simon quotient all-m formula counts insertion orbit types under complete finite separation data, not their Boolean adjacency traces. A surjection from insertion positions to binary crossing vectors can collapse many types, so even a sharp count of all insertion positions cannot yield the claimed lower bound. General Johnson/Hamming VC-density bounds apply to different graph families.

value.rationale: Worst-case number of distinct adjacency neighborhoods over m named vertices is a natural quantitative refinement of VC dimension in finite model theory and learning. The known VCdim-four result gives only quartic Sauer-Shelah growth; a chord gap count gives a quadratic upper bound, but no matching construction. The explicit near-saturated family rigorously identifies the optimal quadratic exponent and sharp leading constant, with an exact arbitrary-size structural spectrum of its output binary run types.
